summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with no relevant personal or family history and normal bowel habits until the end of 2019 had a severe depressive episode, began chlorprothixene, lorazepam, zolpidem and mirtazapine in June 2020, and days later developed severe acute cramping abdominal pain without fever, vomiting or diarrhea. Clinical and biological evaluation were normal and COVID-19 was ruled out; emergency CT showed a 4-cm jejunal-loop tissue mass with wall thickening and a normal-appearing pancreas. Pancreatic tumor and jejunal lymphoma were ruled out by MRI and laparoscopy in July 2020; laparoscopy identified an internal right para-duodenal hernia, which was reduced with closure of the anterior para-duodenal window.

After surgery she had increasing abdominal pain, bloating, alternating constipation and diarrhea with Bristol VII stools, 2–4 kg weight loss and a generalized burning sensation. An extensive workup until 2023 (Table 1) was largely marked Negative/Normal, with exceptions including a gastric antral microfocus of complete intestinal metaplasia, colonic coprostasis, positive H. pylori treated with confirmed eradication, Blastocystis treated with metronidazole, a C. jejuni PCR-positive/antigen-negative colonizer finding and a positive lactulose breath test. Workup concluded severe IBS-C with overflow diarrhea and hypersensitive esophagus; many therapies yielded no clinical response.

With IBS-SSS above 300 and a high quality-of-life burden, a multidisciplinary meeting proposed three experimental oral FMTs, given from the same donor after 5 days of vancomycin and bowel cleansing. One month after FMT symptoms improved with abdominal pain alleviated; at four months diarrhea and abdominal pain improved with an IBS-SSS fall of over 175 points and at least 40% quality-of-life increase, and bowel habits were stable. Improvement persisted beyond 12 months with only the burning sensation persisting. Serial stool 16S sequencing (pre-FMT and 1, 4 and 6 months post-FMT, donor material as reference) showed patient-specific core genera at 20% pre-FMT, Akkermansia falling from nearly 20% to below 1% at 4 months, Dialister and Phascolarctobacterium reversing from 15.55% and 0.01% to 0.01% and 7.07% at 6 months, and Prevotella near one-fifth at 1 month then almost gone by 4 months.
